CHROMIUM: Add CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_PERMISSIVE_DONTAUDIT It's still useful to have SECURITY_SELINUX_DEVELOP=y by default so that external developers can set their machines to developer mode and set permissive SELinux without having to re-build their kernels, but it's still useful to have it not spam the logs by default due to Chrome OS' large number of permissive rules. This change adds a new flag that lets the user control whether or not to log permissive "denials". Signed-off-by: Luis Hctor Chvez <lhchavez@google.com> BUG=b:33437013 TEST=build with USE=selinux_develop, see lots of logs Change-Id: I53a877ba99ebc4eb040cd7b8c916b0bc3ba48a73 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/424948 Commit-Ready: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Tested-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Platform: x86 : chromeos_laptop - Add caroline support Caroline has a PEN_EJECT signal that is routed to 2 CPU GPIO pins: B15: This is used for wakeup (configured by ACPI) B19: We need an input driver to use this to emit SW_PEN_INSERTED event. (This patch enables the B19 usecase). Kevin uses gpio-keys driver to do this but the driver only understands device trees or platform data. Hence we instantiate the gpio-keys with the platform data. It tries to find the GPIO by finding the right Intel gpio_chip and pin 43 (B19) under that chip. I contemplated doing this exactly like it is done for I2C devices currently (thought of introducing a array of platform_devices in the chromeos_laptop structure and instantiating them in chromeos_laptop_probe()). But since I wanted to search for gpio chip, hence I added a platform_init() hook. BUG=chrome-os-partner:59763 TEST=Verify that the "stylus tools" menu gets launched when I eject the pen on caroline. Change-Id: Iac645accb0a6687640c7ef48487f99ae4cf44bb5 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/424941 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: LSM: Add support for symlink traversal policy. This change adds functionality to the chromiumos LSM to pin inodes and associate tracking information with them. This allows tracking symlink traversal policy for an inode. Whenever the FS layer follows a link, it calls out to the LSM, which can then check whether a symlink traversal policy has been set on any directory on the path in question. If a policy is set and it specifies that symlink traversal should be blocked, the corresponding FS system call will fail with EPERM. Note that readlink() continues to work, so userspace may resort to resolving symlinks manually if desired. Symlink traversal policy is configured via securityfs. Files in /sys/kernel/security/chromiumos/symlink_policy/ are used to set the symlink traversal policy: * .../allow: Write a path to the file to set the symlink traversal policy for corresponding inode to "allow". * .../block: Write a path to the file to set the symlink traversal policy for corresponding inode to "block". * .../reset: Write a path to clear the symlink traversal policy for the corresponding inode. * .../flush: Write a path to clear symlink traversal policy for the entire file system the corresponding inode belongs to. Note that this may affect paths outside the subtree corresponding to the specified path (e.g. parents, siblings, or parts of the file system not visible in the affected (bind) mount). BUG=chromium:655606 TEST=Set symlink traversal policy and test paths containing symlinks. Change-Id: I844b2aedd7f022d97d28b074d5e98450b66c6992 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/422333 Commit-Ready: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

charge_state_v2: Correct Smart battery charging/discharging status AverageTimeToFull() and AverageTimeToEmpty() are the predicted time based on the AverageCurrent(), these do not reflect the instant time of charging or discharging. Hence we observe huge number of time (1092h because register has 65535) to full time when battery starts accepting current upon reaching 100%. To overcome this issue, explicitly checking if the AverageTimeToFull() and AverageTimeToEmpty() register values are updated with the valid data. BUG=chrome-os-partner:60802 BRANCH=none TEST=Manually tested on Reef. Charge the battery to 100%, once the battery starts accepting current again observed time to full is not huge number. Change-Id: I6d6c21b72ab824dbe47e44e1e77f1c5319ac2720 Signed-off-by: Vijay Hiremath <vijay.p.hiremath@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/425324 Commit-Ready: Vijay P Hiremath <vijay.p.hiremath@intel.com> Tested-by: Vijay P Hiremath <vijay.p.hiremath@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org>

If any of USB properties that are part of card info is not properly initialized (which was the case when reading USB system attributes failed), stable ID will be derived from unpredictable data - and end up being unstable across reboots.
